style: point the listener to one word to listen for

candidates.angle: jnana yajna, a sacrifice of knowledge, as worship
candidates.evidence: ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः (by that one I may be worshipped through the sacrifice of knowledge, that is my view)

candidates.angle: whoever studies this dialogue is worshipping me
candidates.evidence: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः ... तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः (whoever will study this sacred dialogue of us two ... by that one I may be worshipped, that is my view)

candidates.angle: the dialogue itself becomes a sacrifice to Krishna
candidates.evidence: ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः (worshipped by that one through the sacrifice of knowledge)

angle_en: Jnana yajna, a sacrifice of knowledge

en.intro: Listen for the word yajna. You might expect a blood sacrifice or a fire offering, but Krishna names a very different kind of offering.
en.notice: Yajna is a sacrifice, and Krishna calls the study of this dialogue a jnana yajna, a sacrifice of knowledge. He says that anyone who reads these words is worshipping him directly.
en.next: Krishna then says that even listening to this dialogue with trust frees a person from evil and leads to heaven.
en.meaning: Whoever studies this sacred dialogue of ours will also worship me through the sacrifice of knowledge; that is my view.

hi.intro: यज्ञ शब्द सुनिए। आप किसी आहुति या अग्नि की कल्पना कर सकते हैं, लेकिन कृष्ण एक अलग ही प्रकार के यज्ञ की बात करते हैं।
hi.meaning: जो मनुष्य हम दोनों के इस धर्ममय संवाद का अध्ययन करेगा, उसके द्वारा भी मैं ज्ञानयज्ञ से पूजित होऊँगा ऐसा मेरा मत है।
hi.notice: यज्ञ का अर्थ है आहुति, और कृष्ण इस संवाद को ज्ञानयज्ञ कहते हैं। वे कहते हैं कि जो कोई इन शब्दों का अध्ययन करेगा, वह सीधे उनकी पूजा कर रहा है।
hi.next: कृष्ण आगे कहते हैं कि जो इसे श्रद्धा से सुनता है वह भी पाप से मुक्त होकर पुण्य लोक को जाता है।
